story: Lesson 17 puts the unit to work, over two days. Students plan a painting job: wall area, paint from a rate, cost with a coupon, and time with percentages. Day 1 is the warm-up and the wall area, ending when the class agrees on 300 square feet. Day 2 opens at the release: paint, cost, the coupon and the discussion, then 17.3.
previous: In Lesson 16 students found what percentage one number is of another; today they use that, and unit rates, in one project.

clo.imGoal: Apply rates and percentages to calculate how long it will take and how much it will cost to complete a painting project, and explain (orally) the reasoning.
clo.form: I need ___ quarts, because ___ quarts cover ___ square feet, and two coats is ___ square feet. Buying ___ costs $___, so the total cost is $___.

board.content: We will use rates and percentages to find what a painting project costs.
board.language: We will explain, out loud, how we found the cost, using “square feet,” “cover” and “total cost.”

clo.exemplar: I need 7 quarts, because 7 quarts cover 612.5 square feet, and two coats is 600 square feet. Buying 1 gallon and 3 quarts costs $67.60, so the total cost is $87.60.
clo.lookFor: Each student’s written answer to 17.3’s first question: the friend is not quite right. The east wall is 72 of 300 square feet, so \(\frac{72}{300} \boldcdot 100 = 24\%\), not 25%. Finding 1% first (3 square feet) also counts.

posted.sentence: I need 5 quarts, because 5 quarts cover 450 square feet, and two coats is 400 square feet. Buying 5 quarts costs $40, so the total cost is $55.

clo.progressionNote: IM’s unit overview lists “interpret” and “justify” for this lesson. The objective follows the lesson’s own goal: “explain.”

Some groups add a cost for each item. IM: hardware stores sell painting kits (brushes, rollers, a tray, a drop sheet) for around $20.

Tool names (roller, drop cloth, painter’s tape) may be new words.
misconceptions: Listing only paint, because the job is unfamiliar.
Adding a price for the paint now; IM leaves that until the amount is known.

activities.grouping: Small groups, each with at least one student who has painted, if possible. IM: poll the class first.
activities.monitor: Listen for tools beyond paint. Record the class list, with costs where you can, and keep it up all lesson.

strategies: Area, wall by wall: east 72, south 65 (80 minus the 15 square foot window), west 51 (72 minus the 21 square foot door). North 76, small wall 36. Total 300 square feet.
Paint: 2 quarts per 175 square feet is 87.5 square feet per quart. Two coats is 600 square feet, so about 6.86 quarts: buy 7.
Containers: 7 quarts ($76.30), 2 gallons ($69.80), or 1 gallon and 3 quarts ($67.60). With IM’s $20 kit: $96.30, $89.80 or $87.60.
Coupon, 20% off quarts only: 7 quarts gives $81.04; 1 gallon and 3 quarts gives $81.06; 2 gallons stays $89.80.
barriers: Floor plans may be new: which lines are walls, the door, the window, the closet.
Mixed units: yards for two walls, feet for the rest; quarts and gallons for paint.
Words such as “coats,” “mirrored closet doors” and “floor-to-ceiling.”
misconceptions: Leaving out a surface: the small wall, the 3 square feet above the door, or the wall above and below the window.
Multiplying yards by feet: 3 × 8 for the east wall.
Planning paint for one coat only, from 300 square feet.
Language: “Ours is right, theirs is wrong,” with no reason for either total.
backPocket: Walk me around the room. Which surfaces get paint?
How many coats? How much wall does that make?
Can both be right? What did each one buy?
activities.grouping: Pairs: quiet think time alone on the area, then partners compare. Class agrees on the area, then each student finishes alone.
activities.monitor: IM: notice who organizes their work methodically and who needs help. Track each pair’s area, then each student’s containers and total.

dependsOn.note: IM’s cost answers include the $20 painting kit from 17.1’s closing. If you skip 17.1, give students that price before question 3.

strategies: Divide, then multiply by 100: \(\frac{72}{300} \boldcdot 100\) is 24%, so the friend is not quite right.
1% first: 3 square feet is 1%, so 72 square feet is 24%.
Time: 96 minutes for 24% is 4 minutes per 1%. The other 76% takes 304 minutes alone, so the friend saved 304 − 150, or 154 minutes.
barriers: 17.3 needs 17.2’s 300 square feet and the east wall’s 72.
“25% finished” is about the painting, not the time.
misconceptions: Counting drying time between coats; the problem counts painting time only.
Saying 25% because the east wall is one of four walls.
Subtracting 150 from 96, or from 400, instead of from the time alone for the rest.

release.successCriteria: Name the paint you need and the square feet it covers for two coats, the containers you buy, and the total cost.
release.say: Say how much paint, using the rate. Then say how you got your total cost.
talkMoments: Before the coupon question, partners take turns explaining their total cost with Today’s frame.
In the closing discussion, students who chose different containers each explain their total.

emerging.frame: I need ___ quarts. ___ quarts cover ___ square feet. Two coats is ___ square feet. Buying ___ costs $___. The total cost is $___.
emerging.stretch: They say why they need more paint than one coat.
emerging.nonverbal: They point to the area, then the ad’s rate, then the containers they chose, in order.

developing.frame: I need ___ quarts, because ___ quarts cover ___ square feet, and two coats is ___ square feet. Buying ___ costs $___, so the total cost is $___. I chose those containers because ___.
developing.stretch: They say why a different total can also be right.
developing.nonverbal: They draw arrows from the area to the quarts to the cost, and label each arrow with its unit.

expanding.frame: I need ___ quarts, because ___ quarts cover ___ square feet, and two coats is ___ square feet. Buying ___ costs $___, so the total cost is $___. Another way to buy it is ___, which costs $___.
expanding.stretch: They explain how the coupon changes which containers to buy.
expanding.nonverbal: They write the chain area, paint, cost, with a unit on each step, before they speak.

steps: Ask 1–2 students how much paint they needed. Scribe their words as said, such as “two coats.” Write “cover” and “square feet” beside them.
Poll IM’s cost ranges: $80–$84.99, $85–$89.99, $90–$94.99, $95–$99.99, $100 or more. Then ask, “Can all of these values be correct?”
After quiet think time, call 2–3 students with different containers. Scribe each total as said, with the containers beside it.
Write “total cost” beside their words. Ask how the coupon changes the best buy; students decide, and you scribe.
Leave the board up for 17.3 and the close of the lesson.
synthesis.prompt: Can all of these values be correct? How?
synthesis.sounds: Yes, because each one buys enough paint in different containers. I need 7 quarts, because 7 quarts cover 612.5 square feet, and two coats is 600 square feet. notes: How students might solve it, wall by wall (ceiling 8 ft):
East: 3 yd is 9 ft, and 9 × 8 = 72. It runs the full depth, closet included.
South: 10 × 8 = 80, minus the 5 × 3 window: 65.
West: 9 × 8 = 72, minus the 7 × 3 door: 51.
North: the unlabeled stretch is 10 − 0.5 − 6.5 = 3 ft. With the 6.5 ft closet back, (3 + 6.5) × 8 = 76.
Small wall: two 2 ft sides and the 0.5 ft end, so 16 + 16 + 4 = 36. Total: 300 square feet.
Paint: two coats is 600 square feet. At 87.5 square feet per quart, that is about 6.86 quarts, so buy 7.
Containers: 7 quarts, 2 gallons, or 1 gallon and 3 quarts. Add IM’s $20 kit for the total cost.
Coupon: 20% off the quarts only, so 2 gallons doesn’t change.

beforeClass: This lesson runs over two days. Day 1: 17.1, then 17.2 until the class agrees on 300 square feet. Day 2: 17.2 from the release, then 17.3.
Work 17.2 yourself: the area, the paint for two coats, and two ways to buy it, with and without the coupon.
Find a floor plan of your classroom to display, and a short video of someone painting, in case few students have painted.
For Three Reads in 17.2: display the bedroom plan and its list, with the four questions covered until the third read. Have a marker to add quantities to the plan.
For Collect and Display (MLR 2): clear board space, and have IM’s cost ranges ready to poll: $80–$84.99, $85–$89.99, $90–$94.99, $95–$99.99, $100 or more.

cuts.note: Keep it short: one class list, and IM’s $20 painting kit for supplies. Skip the warm-up only if you give students the $20 kit price.
If short of time, do the first question only: is the friend right about 25%? Lost: the time saved, which uses 24% again.

Two days. Card minutes count IM’s 35 across both: Day 1 ends near minute 20, once the class agrees on 300 square feet. Day 1’s quiet think time on the area is about 7 minutes, not IM’s 15; give all 15 if Day 1 has room. On Day 2, if the cost work runs long, hear two totals, not three. Never cut the closing discussion.

ideas: A real project takes steps: the area first, then the paint, then the cost.
A rate links them: 2 quarts per 175 square feet tells how much paint 600 square feet needs.
A percentage compares a part with the whole: the east wall’s 72 of 300 square feet is 24% of the job.
lessonSynthesis.pointTo: Point to the 17.2 board: the different totals and students’ words for how each was found. If you taught 17.3, point to the 24%.

check.question: A fence has 250 square feet to stain, and it needs two coats. One quart of stain covers 120 square feet and costs $12. A brush costs $10. What does the job cost, and why?
check.sounds: I need 5 quarts, because 5 quarts cover 600 square feet, and two coats is 500 square feet. Buying 5 quarts costs $60, so the total cost is $70.
